item.title: Tomorrows meeting in Naas cancelled due to cold snap
item.description: The weather has also caused the cancelation of tomorrow's racing action at Naas. A frozen track means the 7 racecard will not go ahead with the fixture rescheduled for next Friday. Advertisement

item.title: O'Byrne Cup game decided by coin toss!
item.description: The O'Byrne Cup game between Westmeath and Longford was called off today due to an unplayable pitch. Since a replay wasn't possible, a coin toss decided that Westmeath would progress to the next round while Longford go into the semi finals of the O'Byrne Shield. Advertisement

item.description: It will be a Kerry double header in Croker next Sunday as Ballymacelligott dispatched Grangenolvin in Rathkeale today It was a great start for the Kerry side, scoring 2 goals in the opening few minutes. Ballymac led by 2-5 to 0-9 at half time, but the Kildare side weren't giving up. item.title: Status yellow warning for ice and low temperatures in place for the county
item.description: A status yellow warning for ice and low temperatures will be in place for the county from 6 o'clock. The warning will remain in place until 11 o'clock tomorrow morning. Met Éireann is warning of sharp or severe frost and icy stretches, as temperatures fall to -2 to -4 degrees in some areas. Advertisement Kerry County Council has warned that dangerous traveling conditions are expected and motorists are advised to exercise caution. item.title: Wolves secure first win of the season to double their points tally in Premier League
item.description: John McGinn scored twice for Aston Villa as they beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 to move up to second in the Premier League. Arsenal will extend their lead at the top with victory over Bournemouth in the teatime kick-off. Wolves secured their first win of the season, hammering fellow strugglers West Ham 3-nil at Molineux. Advertisement Burnley's poor form continued, as they went down 2-nil away at Brighton.

item.title: Clare beat Limerick, Tipp and Waterford draw
item.description: All-Ireland champions Tipperary kicked off their year with a draw in the Munster Senior League this afternoon. Waterford came from behind to leave the game level 1-18 each at the full time whistle in Fethard. Clare got the better of neighbours Limerick by 3-20 to 3-18 in Tulla. Advertisement

item.title: Dubs start season with victory in O'Byrne Cup
item.description: The O'Byrne Cup game between Westmeath and Longford was called off today due to an unplayable pitch. Since a replay wasn't possible, a coin toss decided that Westmeath would progress to the next round while Longford go into the semi finals of the O'Byrne Shield. Elsewhere in the cup, Kildare beat Wexford 2-12 to 0-9. Advertisement Meath got past Wicklow 2-11 to 1-12. Dublin got the better of Laois 4-14 and 1-17 and Carlow fell to a 3-14 to 3-9 loss to Offaly.

item.title: Dingle book spot in All Ireland Final
item.description: In another incredible game of football, Dingle have booked their spot in the All Ireland Senior Club Football final thanks to a 1-26 to 1-24 victory over Dublin's Ballyboden St Ends in Cork this evening. Dingle had a lot of work to do in the second half as they trailed 14 points to 5 at the short whistle. Dingle did have a goal disallowed in the opening half. Ballyboden netted 5 minutes into the second half to increase their lead to 10 points but Dingle never gave up. Advertisement Tadhg Browne
